sponsor_or_proposer: National Oil Corporation (NOC) / General Electricity Company of Libya (GECOL)
current_state: NOC chairman Masoud Suleiman and GECOL general manager Abdullah Hammouda discussed 'the possibility of establishing platforms for supplying liquefied gas to the plants' (plus additional fuel storage tanks) to keep power stations running amid chronic gas-supply shortfalls. Concept-stage talks only; consistent with Libya's wider gas squeeze (Gecol fleet short of feedstock) that Bouri gas (2026) and Structures A&E (from 2026) are meant to ease from the supply side.
missing_threshold_elements: No site, no capacity, no vessel/FSRU or unit design, no developer/tender, no timeline — a ministerial-level idea, well below the add bar. Also ambiguous whether 'liquefied gas' means marine LNG import (in scope) or domestic LPG/LNG logistics (out of scope); scope must be resolved before any staging.
watch_for: A named site/port (Tripoli, Benghazi, Misrata?), an FSRU/FSU charter or import-terminal tender, a GECOL power-plant conversion tied to imported LNG, or NOC budget/board approval. Note separately: Marsa El Brega remains mothballed (no LNG-export restart; 2026 tanker-arrival news at Brega is LPG/products logistics, not LNG).
notes: Lead URL verified (url_verifier token 'platforms' PASS). Upstream oil-operator sweep (SOP §4.3) found gas-monetization signals — Farigh–Brega 130-km flared-gas pipeline trial (Apr 2026), Bouri gas start-up, Eni/NOC Structures A&E — but all feed the domestic grid/Mellitah pipeline exports (Greenstream), not any new LNG liquefaction or FLNG proposal.
